response.headline: Three-Week Plateau Despite a Real 246 kcal Deficit
response.narrative:
You lost 5.54 lbs in the first two weeks of this cycle at an average intake of roughly 1,709 kcal/day, which was aggressive and effective. From W4 onward your weekly average weight has barely moved — 215.3, 215.0, and 215.1 lbs — essentially flat for three consecutive weeks. Unlike a typical calorie-creep stall, this one isn't explained by rising intake: your most recent two-week average is 1,766 kcal/day, only 56 kcal above your W1–W2 baseline of 1,709 kcal/day. At your estimated TDEE of 2,011 kcal/day, you're still running a genuine ~246 kcal daily deficit — enough to expect roughly 0.35 lbs of loss per week on paper. The scale disagreeing with a real deficit like this points toward metabolic adaptation or water retention masking fat loss, rather than a logging or intake problem.

Protein is the other piece worth fixing here — you've averaged only 180–185g across every week this cycle, consistently below the ~224g minimum recommended for your current bodyweight of 212.9 lbs (roughly 1g per lb). Low protein during an extended deficit increases the risk of losing lean mass, which would only suppress your BMR further and make this plateau harder to break. Carbs and fats have moved together with total intake in a fairly controlled band (124–165g carbs, 50–58g fats), so protein is the one number that actually needs to move.

The positive signal here is your waist measurement: a 0.5-inch drop between 2026-07-22 and 2026-07-25 suggests body recomposition is still occurring even while the scale is stuck. You are not in a metabolic crisis — cutting further right now risks chasing a deficit that's already real. The more useful move is holding steady (or a short structured refeed) and giving the plateau time to resolve before tightening intake again.

With 7 weeks remaining in your cycle ending 2026-09-13, you have enough runway to reach 200 lbs even after a short hold. Both paths below keep you at or below your current baseline while raising protein to 224g minimum — not cutting further into an already-real deficit — with the aggressive path pushing moderately below baseline once the plateau breaks, and the sustainable path holding at baseline and leaning on a steps increase instead of a deeper cut.
response.primaryAction: Hold intake at or just below your baseline (~1,700 kcal) rather than cutting further this week — the deficit is already real, so the priority is ruling out adaptation, not widening the gap.
response.secondaryAction: Bring protein up to 224g minimum and hold it there every day — it's been under target all cycle and matters more right now than cutting calories further.

sustainable.label: Sustainable
sustainable.rationale: Holding intake at baseline (~1,700 kcal) while raising protein to 224g minimum protects lean mass during the plateau, with a progressive steps ramp adding activity instead of widening an already-real deficit.
sustainable.summary: Week 1 holds at your existing baseline of 1,700 kcal and 10,000 steps, while protein increases to 224g minimum — no further calorie cut, since the deficit already checks out. Weeks 2–4 continue at the same intake and protein target. Week 5 is a full diet-break week at 2,050 kcal (protein still 224g) to actively rule out adaptive suppression. The final two weeks return to the 1,700 kcal baseline with steps increased to 12,000/day, using activity rather than further restriction to close out the cycle.

aggressive.label: Aggressive
aggressive.rationale: A moderate cut to just below baseline (~1,550 kcal, still well short of your old 1,500 kcal low) with protein raised to 224g minimum and a progressive steps ramp to 14,000 gives a realistic shot at 200 lbs by September 13, without stacking an extreme cut or continued low protein on top of a deficit that's already real.
aggressive.summary: Week 1 continues at your current level while data confirms the plateau is adaptation, not creep. Weeks 2–5 move to 1,550 kcal — below baseline, but a moderate step down rather than a shock cut — with protein raised to 224g minimum and steps rising to 12,000/day. Week 6 is a refeed week at 1,950 kcal (protein held at 224g) to manage adaptation risk before the final week, which holds 1,550 kcal and pushes steps to 14,000/day for the cycle finish.

response._revisionNote: You're right on both counts — I made an error setting the Week 1 steps target at 8,000 when your logged data shows you've been consistently hitting above that, and I failed to structure a progressive steps increase toward the end of the sustainable path to widen the deficit in the final weeks. I'm revising both paths now to correct this.
